solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: OK for outing, I'm fond of fruit

indicators.note: an outing here is a putting-out, so the named letters are expelled from the phrase

blocks.note: I am fond = one likes, with 'one' standing for the speaker
the two letters to be taken out, as written

explanation.surface: Someone gives the go-ahead for a day out and declares a love of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove O and K from ONE LIKES to leave NELIES. 'OK' looks like approval but is just the two letters to lose.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelis is a kind of winter pear, and NELIES is a Chambers plural, so the word names pieces of fruit.

clue.text: Note saving energy gets small bills

indicators.note: saving here means keeping safe within, so the first part holds the other

blocks.note: NB, nota bene, means note well
E is the symbol for energy
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Cutting back on power use brings lower utility bills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bills' reads as invoices but means birds' beaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A neb is a Scots and northern word for a beak or bill of a bird.

clue.text: Lively dance item, new out sparkled

indicators.note: lively suggests bouncing energetically about, so the letters are jumbled up
out means put outside, so that letter is removed from the fodder

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new, the letter taken away

explanation.surface: A spirited dance number with fresh moves really shone.
explanation.walkthrough: Without N, the letters of DANCE ITEM rearrange to EMICATED.
explanation.definitionFit: To emicate is a rare Chambers verb meaning to sparkle or glitter, from Latin emicare, to flash out.

clue.text: Urges chancellor to share data run on head of state

indicators.note: to share something is to take part in it, so this piece goes in among the other letters
'head of' keeps only the first letter of 'state'

blocks.note: info is short for information, data
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
CE abbreviates Chancellor of the Exchequer
first letter of state

explanation.surface: A Chancellor of the Exchequer presses for sharing information with the head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chancellor of the Exchequer is the UK finance minister. 'Share' reads as a verb about data, but it tells the chancellor's letters to go in among the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Inforce is an old Chambers spelling of enforce, and to enforce is to urge or press a point.

clue.text: Arms taken up in American party

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking something up lifts it bottom to top, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: gat is American slang for a gun, so gats are arms

explanation.surface: Weapons are brought out at a party in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In American' tells us the slang is American: gat is US underworld slang for a pistol.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is short for a stag party, a men-only celebration held before a wedding.

clue.text: Gazelles in uplands heard

indicators.note: something heard is taken in by the ear, so the word is judged by its sound alone

blocks.note: moors are high open uplands

explanation.surface: Antelopes are spotted grazing in hill country.
explanation.walkthrough: Moors are heathland uplands; the answer is pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The mhorr is a West African gazelle, a rare antelope listed in Chambers.

clue.text: Thinks over liquor regularly for lines of verse

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
one word spread over another covers it, so the first goes round the second

blocks.note: to muse is to think or ponder
the second, fourth and sixth letters of liquor

explanation.surface: A poet ponders a drink and keeps returning to lines of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liquor' looks like part of the picture of a drinking poet, but only its even letters are used. 'Over' works as a container here, not a sign of reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A miurus is a dactylic hexameter with a short penultimate syllable, a kind of line in classical verse.

clue.text: Husband's rarely gone for strong drink

indicators.note: rarely here suggests in an unusual or strange way, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
taken as written

explanation.surface: A husband has seldom gone out for a stiff drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rarely' reads as an adverb of frequency, but is the shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogen, short for hogen-mogen, is an archaic word for a potent liquor, so it is a strong drink.

clue.text: Conductor upset some in rickety vehicle

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads bottom to top

blocks.note: Sir Simon Rattle, the British orchestral conductor
some, as in a part or portion of something

explanation.surface: A conductor is shaken up while riding in a ramshackle old bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' suggests a bus conductor in the surface; it is Simon Rattle, longtime head of the Berlin Philharmonic and the London Symphony Orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattletrap is a shaky, worn-out old car or carriage that rattles as it goes.

clue.text: Wasp-like flies worried shipyards? Admiralty's leader leaving

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of the word is wanted
something leaving departs, so that letter is taken out of the fodder
worried in the sense of shaken about, as a dog worries a bone, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of Admiralty, which leaves

explanation.surface: Insects bother dockyard workers once the naval chief has departed.
explanation.walkthrough: Take one A out of SHIPYARDS and rearrange what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Syrphids are hoverflies, many of which mimic the yellow and black banding of wasps.

clue.text: Emerging general after English degree

indicators.note: coming after puts the general's word behind the other two pieces rather than in clue order

blocks.note: E is the standard abbreviation for English
Master of Arts, a university degree
general, as in nationwide, applying to the whole country

explanation.surface: A general appears on the scene after taking an English degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like an army officer, but here it is the adjective meaning nationwide; 'after' puts it behind E and MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Emanational describes what flows out or issues forth, so it matches something emerging from a source.

clue.text: One trick absorbed by commoner with craft of an old Greek

indicators.note: something absorbed is soaked up inside, so these letters go within the other word

blocks.note: more common, more hackneyed: triter is the comparative of trite
a, the indefinite article, means one
a con is a swindle or trick

explanation.surface: A common man pulls off a trick with an ancient Greek ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commoner' reads as a person not of noble rank, but it is the comparative adjective, meaning more hackneyed.
explanation.definitionFit: A triaconter was an ancient Greek galley rowed by thirty oars, so it is a vessel of the classical world.

clue.text: Stokes dismissed in carnage after fine cutting

indicators.note: a batsman who is dismissed leaves the field, so this letter departs from the word
placing one part after another tells us the order in which the two parts are laid side by side

blocks.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
carnage is mass killing
S is the symbol for stokes, a unit of viscosity, which loses its place

explanation.surface: England cricketer Ben Stokes is out amid a batting collapse after some fine play.
explanation.walkthrough: Stokes reads as the cricketer, which makes 'dismissed' feel natural; it is really the unit stokes, abbreviated S.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaughter is a Scots word for paring or cutting turf from the ground with a broad spade.

clue.text: Fish bones more than once inspiring recipe from the east

indicators.note: to inspire is to breathe in, so the outer word takes the other inside it
in an across clue, reading from the east means right to left, backwards

blocks.note: Bones (sawbones) is slang for a doctor; more than once makes it plural
R is the prescription abbreviation for recipe, Latin for take

explanation.surface: A fish dish keeps getting bony bits, so the cook consults an Eastern recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes into DOCS after the O to make DORCS, which read backwards gives SCROD.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrod is a young cod or haddock, especially as sold split and cooked in New England.

clue.text: Republican journo is against the Crown for tabloid

blocks.note: R is the standard abbreviation for Republican
ED, short for editor, a newspaper journalist
the crown of anything is its top

explanation.surface: An anti-monarchist journalist writes for a popular newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Crown' looks like the monarchy but simply means the top of something. In crosswords 'against' often means next to.
explanation.definitionFit: A red-top is a British downmarket newspaper, so called from the red mastheads of papers like the Sun and Mirror.

clue.text: Gypsy was anxious for an audience

indicators.note: an audience listens rather than reads, so we go by how the word sounds

blocks.note: to care is to be anxious or concerned

explanation.surface: A traveller felt nervous facing a crowd of listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: Caird is a Scots word for a travelling tinker or vagrant, used of a gypsy.

clue.text: Charge lady for herbaceous plant

blocks.note: a charge is a price or cost
Mary, a common woman's name, here for any lady

explanation.surface: A woman is billed for a garden plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' tempts towards heraldry, and a rose is a heraldic charge, giving the false trail ROSEMARY; the crossing letters kill it.
explanation.definitionFit: Costmary is an aromatic perennial herb of the daisy family, once used to flavour ale.

clue.text: Indian mercenaries busy in raids following pressure

indicators.note: busy suggests bustling activity, so the letters are stirred about
following means coming after, which fixes which piece goes first

blocks.note: P is the symbol for pressure
taken as written

explanation.surface: Hired soldiers keep busy launching raids under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pindaris were irregular horsemen and plunderers in 18th and 19th century India, attached to Maratha armies as mercenaries.

clue.text: Note a university charging without extras is appropriate for artisans

indicators.note: charging means loading or filling, as one charges a gun, so the other letters are packed inside

blocks.note: basic means plain, with no extras
N is the abbreviation for note
taken as written
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A university that charges a basic fee is suited to working craftsmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charging' suggests fees in the surface, but here it means loading, as one charges a gun with powder.
explanation.definitionFit: Banausic means mechanical or merely utilitarian, describing manual work fit for a craftsman rather than a gentleman.

clue.text: One involved in rationing, Attlee left nothing out

indicators.note: out here means out of order or wrong, so the letters must be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: The postwar Labour leader Attlee, who presided over rationing, gave nothing away.
explanation.walkthrough: Clement Attlee led the Labour government of 1945 to 1951, when wartime rationing continued, which makes 'left' read as political.
explanation.definitionFit: An allottee is a person to whom a share is allotted, as anyone receiving a ration is.

clue.text: Old PM has day alongside Middle Easterner

blocks.note: D is the standard abbreviation for day
a person from Israel

explanation.surface: A former prime minister spends a day with a visitor from the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: Benjamin Disraeli, Victorian prime minister, was himself of Jewish descent, which makes the surface neat.
explanation.definitionFit: Disraeli was British Prime Minister twice in the nineteenth century, hence an old PM.

clue.text: Distinguished conservative Eden involved with research briefly

indicators.note: involved in its sense of tangled or intricate, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
taken as written
RES is the short form of research

explanation.surface: Anthony Eden, the eminent Tory, took part in some brief research.
explanation.walkthrough: Anthony Eden was a Conservative prime minister, which makes 'Distinguished conservative Eden' read as one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To secern is to discriminate or tell apart, so secerned means distinguished in that sense.

clue.text: Car from Slovakia with advanced exhaust set up?

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting something up raises it, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: SK is the international code for Slovakia
A is the abbreviation for advanced
to do someone in is to exhaust them; do alone can mean wear out

explanation.surface: A car from Slovakia has a modern exhaust system fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: A and DO together are read upwards to give ODA. The question mark admits that the car really comes from the Czech Republic.
explanation.definitionFit: Skoda is a Czech carmaker, so a Skoda is a make of car.

clue.text: Nothing to stop serious disease for a period of about 18 years

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a hole, so this letter goes into the middle of the other word

blocks.note: SARS, severe acute respiratory syndrome
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A long-term programme hopes to halt a grave illness.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes between the A and R of SARS.
explanation.definitionFit: The saros is the eclipse cycle of about 18 years after which the Sun, Moon and Earth return to the same alignment.

clue.text: Island this country accepted as a honey source

blocks.note: the Isle of Man
for a British newspaper, this country is the UK
A is the abbreviation for accepted, as on a bill of exchange

explanation.surface: An island's product is welcomed in Britain as a source of honey.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is a self-governing island in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Manuka is a New Zealand tea tree whose flowers give bees the nectar for prized manuka honey.

clue.text: Sustained popularity on Sabbath

blocks.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
S is the abbreviation for Sabbath

explanation.surface: Something stays in fashion thanks to a Sunday showing.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket field is split into off and on halves, and the on side is also called leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A story or show that has legs keeps going, so legs is idiom for lasting appeal.

clue.text: Spots attacking positions in fencing right away

indicators.note: something sent away is no longer present, so that letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: quart (carte) is the fourth of the parrying and thrusting positions in fencing
R is the abbreviation for right, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A fencer's lunging stances are noticed with the right arm out of play.
explanation.walkthrough: Quart here is not the liquid measure but a fencing position, also spelt carte.
explanation.definitionFit: Quat is an old word for a pimple or pustule, so quats are spots on the skin.

clue.text: People removing top piece with spade making these?

definitions.text: People removing top piece with spade making these?

indicators.note: removing the top piece takes off the head, so the opening letter goes

blocks.note: S is the card-game abbreviation for spade
bods is slang for people

explanation.surface: Gardeners skimming off turf with a spade produce these.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: cutting off the top layer with a spade makes turves.
explanation.definitionFit: Sods are slabs of turf cut from the surface, exactly what is lifted when the top layer is removed with a spade.

clue.text: CD missing in hot cars used for racing? Renault perhaps

indicators.note: whatever is missing is absent, so those two letters are not used
racing suggests careering about wildly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the two letters to be removed, as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Stolen cars with no stereo get raced, maybe a Renault.
explanation.walkthrough: Renault looks like the French carmaker, which fits the racing surface; it is Mary Renault, writer of historical novels such as The King Must Die.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Renault was a woman novelist, an example of an authoress, the old feminine form of author.

clue.text: Composer's woeful dirges filmed with brass?

indicators.note: woeful suggests something in a sorry, wretched state, so the letters are knocked out of shape

blocks.note: Giuseppe Verdi, the Italian opera composer
taken as written

explanation.surface: An opera composer's mournful laments were recorded with a brass section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Filmed' suggests a camera, but here it means coated with a thin film; the question mark admits the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdigris is the green coating that forms on copper and brass, so verdigrised metal is covered with that film.

clue.text: The old bars supply teas

indicators.note: read as supple-ly, in a pliant, bendable way, so the letters are bent into a new order

blocks.note: ye is the archaic form of the, as in Ye Olde Shoppe
taken as written

explanation.surface: Traditional pubs provide afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a verb meaning provide, but it is read as the adverb from supple.
explanation.definitionFit: Yerba, short for yerba mate, is the South American holly whose leaves make a stimulating tea-like drink.

clue.text: Bases of clues not all can see after one second!

indicators.note: not means the following thing is to be excluded, so that letter is left out of the word
placing a part after another sets the order in which the pieces are joined

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for a second
o' is a shortened form of of, as in o'clock
taken as written
a U-rated film is one everybody may see, the letter excluded

explanation.surface: A solver complains that some of the clue foundations are hidden from view at first glance.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for all ages.
explanation.definitionFit: A socle is a plain plinth or block forming the base of a column, statue or wall.
